title: FloodVR headset callouts
description: Response of GET /callouts — LIVE on the Windows tunnel. Short in-headset annotations the VR app renders as an arrow or highlight plus one line of text. Reflects the latest guarded POST /assess run, else a cached no-evidence baseline run; the response bytes are identical between runs, so a poller can diff raw text. Query: ?seen=id1,id2 drops callouts whose callout id or item_id is listed. Server keeps text <= 60 chars (schema allows 90). All text is server-side templates over structured data, never evidence or scene text. position = manifest position raised 0.35 m; absent for scene-text (anchor on the SceneText prop by item_id) and whole-house callouts. kind=missed appears only with ?seen=: damaged items not yet inspected.

audit_trail_id.description: Ties these callouts to the /assess run that produced them.

waterline_m.description: Echoed from house_geometry.json so the app can draw the line without a second fetch.

id.description: Stable callout id, unique within the response.

item_id.description: Damage id from the manifest, or a scene_text id for kind=blocked.

kind.description: hazard = dangerous, do not approach. missed = damage the adjuster has not inspected yet (only returned when ?seen= is given; every damaged line item not in seen). blocked = an injection attempt was caught here (this is the fridge note). measurement = a derived quantity. coverage = a peril/policy determination or a claim-vs-scene conflict.

text.description: ONE line for the headset. Keep under 90 characters — it is read at arm's length through a cardboard lens.

priority.description: 1 renders first and largest. Priority-1 hazards are life-safety.

position.description: World-space metres, same frame as the manifest. Absent when the callout is not anchored to a point.

color.description: red = hazard, amber = blocked injection, blue = measurement/coverage, green = confirmed undamaged.

detail.description: Longer text for a gaze-to-expand panel. The headset shows `text` first.
